subject: r/qtl2 analysis on the CC mice

messages.author: 703654a6137d4f5b
messages.subject: r/qtl2 analysis on the CC mice
parts:
Hi everyone :)

I’m trying to use the r/qtl2 analysis on the CC mice.
The phenotype is in the line level, but the extra data is in the mouse level (age of tumor development, gender and so on).
Is it possible that the phenotype will be as binary file of the CC lines and the covariates file will be with the data by each mouse?
Another question, I can’t find the gene map and genotype data of all the CC lines that I have, but in the r/qtl I used the condensed file with all the markers in the CC lines, can I use it also in the r/qtl2?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: r/qtl2 analysis on the CC mice
parts:
> The phenotype is in the line level, but the extra data is in the mouse level (age of tumor development, gender and so on).
> Is it possible that the phenotype will be as binary file of the CC lines and the covariates file will be with the data by each mouse?

If you want to control for covariates at the individual level, you're maybe going to have to do something that is more complicated than what R/qtl2 provides, and I think you're going to want to use phenotypes measured at the individual level, too.

> Another question, I can’t find the gene map and genotype data of all the CC lines that I have, but in the r/qtl I used the condensed file with all the markers in the CC lines, can I use it also in the r/qtl2?

If you have data in R/qtl1 format, you can load it into R with qtl::read.cross() and then convert it to R/qtl2 format with qtl2::convert2cross2()
The CC genotypes that I have were taken from Srivastava et al. (2017) and are at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/main/CC

karl
